body:
## Summary

`FdG2SwaptionEngine::calculate()` and `FdHullWhiteSwaptionEngine::calculate()` never checked `arguments_.settlementType`/`settlementMethod` at all. Both value a European swaption with `FdmAffineModelSwapInnerValue`, which replicates the exercise payoff from the underlying swap's own cashflows under the short-rate model — the same physical-style payoff a `Physical` and a `Cash`+`CollateralizedCashPrice` settled swaption share by definition. Without a guard, a `Cash`+`ParYieldCurve` swaption — whose payoff genuinely differs (an annuity-based formula this approach doesn't implement) — was silently priced as if it were physically exercised instead of being rejected.

Every other engine valuing a swaption this way already guards with `settlementMethod != Settlement::ParYieldCurve`:

- `JamshidianSwaptionEngine`
- `Gaussian1dJamshidianSwaptionEngine`
- `Gaussian1dSwaptionEngine`
- `Gaussian1dNonstandardSwaptionEngine`
- `Gaussian1dFloatFloatSwaptionEngine`
- `TreeSwaptionEngine`
- `G2SwaptionEngine` (per #2996)

These two finite-difference engines were simply missing the check entirely — a related but distinct defect from #2996 (that one over-rejected a valid input with a loud error; this one silently mis-prices an unsupported one with no error at all).

## Test plan

- Added `testFdSwaptionEnginesCashSettlement` in `test-suite/bermudanswaption.cpp`: for both `FdHullWhiteSwaptionEngine` and `FdG2SwaptionEngine`, prices the same European swaption under `Settlement::Physical` and `Settlement::Cash`+`CollateralizedCashPrice` and checks the NPVs match, and confirms `Cash`+`ParYieldCurve` is now correctly rejected.
- Verified the new test fails without the guard (`"exception Error expected but not raised"` on the `ParYieldCurve` case, for both engines) and passes with the fix.
- Ran the full `BermudanSwaptionTests` suite — all pass.

🤖 Co-worked with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

review_comments.body: This describes the pre-fix behavior as current behavior: both engines now validate `settlementMethod` and reject `ParYieldCurve`, rather than silently pricing it as physical settlement. Please use past tense for the original defect or describe the rejection that this test verifies.

Good catch, fixed in 16fc39471 — reworded to past tense for the original defect and added a sentence stating what the test verifies now (that Physical/Cash+CollateralizedCashPrice still price identically and Cash+ParYieldCurve is rejected).

title: Reject `ParYieldCurve`-settled swaptions in the finite-difference swaption engines
